q: What changes when you say maa with a different tone?
o: Nothing: the tone only shows feeling
The word: มา (come), ม้า (horse) and หมา (dog) are different words
why: In Thai the tone is part of the word, so a new tone gives a new word.

q: Which tone has no mark in the romanization?
why: Only the mid tone is written with no mark: maa, glai.

q: How do you ask a yes/no question in Thai?
o: Raise your voice at the end, as in English
Add ไหม at the end and keep every tone
Say the last word with a high tone
why: ไหม at the end makes the question; the tones of the other words do not change.

q: How is the romanization bp pronounced?
o: Like an English p, with a puff of air
Like a b with tense lips and no puff of air
As two sounds, b and then p
why: bp is a plain p with no puff, which English ears hear as close to b.

q: What does the th in ทา (to paint) sound like?
o: A t with a puff of air, as in top
why: Thai th is always a t with a puff of air, never the th of think.

q: What changes if you say ดู (to look) with a short vowel?
o: It becomes ดุ, a different word
why: Vowel length is part of the word: short ดุ means fierce or to scold.

q: Which polite particle does a woman put at the end of a question?
why: Women end statements with ค่ะ (falling tone) and questions with คะ (high tone).

q: Someone says ขอบคุณครับ to you. What do Thais usually answer?
o: ไม่เป็นไร, or just a smile
why: Thai has no word-for-word you're welcome; ไม่เป็นไร (it's OK) is the usual answer.

q: How do you address Somchai politely?
why: คุณ goes before the first name, for men and women.

q: How do you say 20 in Thai?
why: 20 is ยี่สิบ; สองสิบ is never used.

q: Why is 31 สามสิบเอ็ด and not สามสิบหนึ่ง?
o: A 1 at the end of a bigger number is เอ็ด
หนึ่ง is only for prices
why: หนึ่ง is used alone; at the end of 11, 21, 31… the 1 is เอ็ด.

q: Where does บาท go?
o: Only on price tags, never in speech
After the number: ห้าสิบบาท
Between the tens and the ones
why: The unit follows the number: ห้าสิบบาท, fifty baht.

q: ข and ค both sound kh. What is the difference?
o: ค has no puff of air
Their class, which changes the tone rules
ข is only used at the end of a word
Nothing: they are the same letter
why: ข is high class and ค is low class: same sound, different tone rules.

q: How does written Thai show where a word ends?
o: With a space after every word
It doesn't: words run together, and spaces mark phrases
why: Thai puts no spaces between words; a space ends a phrase.

q: What tone does ขา (leg) have, with a high-class letter, a long vowel and no tone mark?
why: A high-class letter with a long vowel and no tone mark gives a rising tone.

q: In เด็ก (child), what do you say first?
why: เ is written before the consonant but said after it: d, then e, then k.

q: Which pair differs in vowel length?
why: ดุ has a short u and ดู a long one; the short vowel also gives ดุ its low tone.

q: Why is there an อ in อา (aunt) or อาหาร (food)?
o: It is a vowel sound o
It is silent and carries the vowel
why: A syllable that starts with a vowel sound uses the silent อ as its consonant.

q: How does a woman say I in everyday speech?
why: Women say ฉัน, or ดิฉัน when formal; men say ผม.

q: How do you say my friend (male speaker)?
why: The owner comes after the noun: เพื่อนผม.

q: You want to call a server who looks younger than you. What do you say?
o: น้องครับ or น้องคะ
why: น้อง (younger sibling) is the friendly way to address a younger server.

q: How does อาหาร (food) end?
why: Final ร is read n: aa-hǎan.

q: Which syllable is dead?
why: บาท ends in t, so it is dead; the others end in a long vowel, n or w.

q: Why does ราก (root) have a falling tone but รัก (love) a high tone?
o: ราก has a long vowel; with a low-class letter in a dead syllable, long gives falling and short gives high
ราก has a tone mark
why: Low class + dead syllable: long vowel falling, short vowel high.

q: How do you say I'm hungry (male speaker)?
why: Describing words need no เป็น: ผมหิว.

q: Which word says where something is?
why: อยู่ is for place: ห้องน้ำอยู่ที่ไหน.

q: How do you say I'm not a teacher (female speaker)?
why: Before a noun, not is ไม่ใช่ (or ไม่ได้เป็น), never ไม่เป็น.

q: How do you say "two books"?
why: Noun, number, classifier: หนังสือสองเล่ม. The classifier for books is เล่ม.

q: Which classifier counts animals, like cats and dogs?
why: ตัว counts animals, and also shirts, tables and chairs. คน is only for people.

q: You don't know the classifier for a small thing. What can you use?
why: อัน is the safe classifier for small things when you don't know the right one. A number with no classifier is wrong.

q: What tone does ่ give on a low-class letter, as in ไม่ (not)?
why: On a low-class letter, ่ gives a falling tone: ไม่ (mâi).

q: Which tone marks appear only on mid-class letters?
why: ไม้ตรี ๊ and ไม้จัตวา ๋ are used only on mid-class letters, as in โต๊ะ and ก๋วยเตี๋ยว.

q: ม้า (horse): ม is low class and has ้. Which tone?
why: On a low-class letter, ้ gives a high tone: ม้า (máa).

q: How do you say "this shirt"?
why: Noun + classifier + นี้, with a high tone: เสื้อตัวนี้.

q: Which word means "this" standing alone, as in "This is my cat"?
why: นี่, with a falling tone, stands alone; นี้ follows a noun and classifier.

q: How do you say "my house" (male speaker)?
why: The owner comes after the thing: บ้านของผม, or just บ้านผม.

q: Where does ไม่ go in "I don't like coffee"?
o: After the verb: ผมชอบไม่กาแฟ
At the end: ผมชอบกาแฟไม่
Before the verb: ผมไม่ชอบกาแฟ
At the start: ไม่ผมชอบกาแฟ
why: ไม่ goes right before the verb: ไม่ชอบ.

q: Someone asks ชอบไหม (Do you like it?). How do you say yes?
why: Answer with the verb: ชอบ for yes, ไม่ชอบ for no.

q: How do you turn เผ็ด (it's spicy) into a yes/no question?
o: Say เผ็ด with a rising voice
Put ไหม at the end: เผ็ดไหม
Put ไหม at the start: ไหมเผ็ด
Put ไม่ at the end: เผ็ดไม่
why: ไหม at the end makes the question; the voice does not need to rise.

q: In หมา (dog), what does ห do?
o: It is silent and gives ม a rising tone
It adds a short a after it
why: A leading ห is silent and makes the next letter high class, so หมา has a rising tone.

q: Which word starts with a true cluster (two letters said together)?
why: ปลา starts with ป + ล said together; หมา and อยู่ have a silent first letter, and สบาย hides a vowel.

q: How is ตลาด (market) read?
o: As ตะ-หลาด, with a hidden a
As ต-ลาด with a long a in the first syllable
why: A short a is said between ต and ล, and ลาด takes the class of ต.

q: How do you ask "What are you eating?"
why: The question word goes where the answer goes: คุณกินอะไร.

q: Where does กี่ (how many) go?
o: Before the classifier: แมวกี่ตัว
At the start: กี่แมว
After the classifier: แมวตัวกี่
Before the noun: กี่ตัวแมว
why: กี่ takes the place of the number, so it comes before the classifier.

q: Can you add ไหม after a question word?
o: No: the question word already asks
Only after ที่ไหน
why: ไหม is only for yes/no questions; never add it after อะไร, ใคร or ที่ไหน.

q: What does the mark ์ do in เบียร์ (beer)?
why: ์ over a letter means the letter is not said.

q: Which word has a short vowel even though the spelling looks long?
why: เล่น is said short (lên); น้ำ, ได้ and เก้า are said long.

q: What does ๆ do in ช้าๆ?
o: It repeats the word before it
why: ๆ repeats the word: ช้าๆ, slowly.

q: How do you ask for two plates of pad thai (male speaker)?
why: Dish, number, classifier: ผัดไทยสองจาน, with จาน for a plate.

q: Which word means spicy?
why: เผ็ด is spicy; ร้อน is hot to the touch.

q: How do you ask for the bill?
why: เช็คบิลด้วย: check, please. ด้วย softens the request.

q: How do you say "my older sister" (male speaker)?
why: The owner comes after the noun, and พี่ means older: พี่สาวผม.

q: How do you say "I'm thirty years old" (female speaker)?
why: อายุ works like a verb: no เป็น.

q: Which word means a younger brother?
why: น้อง is younger, ชาย is male: น้องชาย.

q: How do you say "more expensive"?
why: กว่า goes right after the describing word, with no word for "more" before it: แพงกว่า.

q: Where does มาก (very) go?
o: At the start of the sentence
why: มาก follows the word it makes stronger: สวยมาก, very beautiful.

q: Which means "the biggest"?
why: ที่สุด after the describing word means "the most": ใหญ่ที่สุด.

q: How do you say 7 p.m.?
why: Evening hours restart at 7 p.m.: หนึ่งทุ่ม is 7 p.m., สองทุ่ม is 8 p.m.

q: How do you say "at 6 a.m." in "I get up at 6 a.m."?
why: Thai needs no word for "at" before a time: ผมตื่นหกโมงเช้า.

q: Where will you mostly see times like สิบสี่นาฬิกา (14:00)?
o: On announcements, tickets and the news
why: The 24-hour นาฬิกา count is formal; in speech people say บ่ายสองโมง.

q: How does Thai show that something happened in the past?
o: With a time word such as เมื่อวาน, or แล้ว for done
With แล้ว after every past verb
With เป็น before the verb
why: Thai verbs never change; a time word, or แล้ว for something finished, shows the past.

q: A friend asks กินข้าวหรือยัง. You haven't eaten. You answer:
why: ยัง means "not yet"; ใช่ only confirms "is it …?".

q: Where does จะ go?
o: At the end of the sentence
why: จะ goes right before the verb: จะไป, will go.

q: What does ได้ไป mean?
o: got to go, had the chance to go
why: ได้ before a verb means "got to"; "can go" is ไปได้.

q: How do you say "I want coffee" (wanting a thing)?
why: To want a thing, use อยากได้ + the thing.

q: Someone asks ว่ายน้ำได้ไหม. You can swim. You answer:
why: Answer a ได้ไหม question with ได้ or ไม่ได้, not with ใช่.

q: Which sounds most natural when you ask a server for the bill?
why: เช็คบิลด้วย, with ครับ or ค่ะ, is the everyday way; กรุณา sounds like a sign.

q: What does ช่วย + verb + หน่อย ask for?
o: Someone to do something for you
A thing you want to have
why: ช่วย … หน่อย is "could you …, please".

q: Where do you mostly meet กรุณา (please)?
why: กรุณา is formal; in speech, Thai uses ขอ, ช่วย and หน่อย.

q: How do you ask "Where is the market?"
why: The place comes first, then อยู่ที่ไหน at the end.

q: What tells ใกล้ (near) and ไกล (far) apart?
o: The tone: falling for near, mid for far
why: ใกล้ has a falling tone, ไกล a mid tone; the consonants and vowel are the same.

q: How do you tell a taxi driver "to Siam"?
why: ไป + place, with no word for "to": ไปสยาม.

q: How do you say "a red shirt"?
why: The color comes after the noun, with สี: เสื้อสีแดง.

q: Which classifier do pants (กางเกง) take?
why: Pants are counted like shirts, with ตัว, even though English says "a pair".

q: Said of clothes, ฟิต means:
why: ฟิต is a false friend: กางเกงตัวนี้ฟิต means the pants are tight.

q: How do you say "I'm tired" (female speaker)?
why: Feelings are describing verbs: no เป็น, ฉันเหนื่อย.

q: Which of these takes เป็น?
why: Illnesses take เป็น: เป็นหวัด. Feelings do not.

q: What does ปวดท้อง mean?
why: ปวด + body part: ท้อง is the belly.
